wouldn't any Dyson Sphere be hard to detect? if we can't see the star how would we know it's there?
In theory? Consistent infrared emissions from an area much larger than a star.

Star's radiation heats up the Dyson sphere, making it hotter than the surrounding space. The Dyson Sphere would be like an oven, where the heat is contained inside, but the outside still radiates a bit of that heat into the external environment. With a powerful enough detector, you can see the infrared radiation emanating from the sphere. At least that's my understanding of it.

With a star like our sun, the Dyson sphere is much larger, collects more radiation from the sun, and emanates more infrared radiation than a sphere around a white dwarf. More infrared means easier to detect than a smaller infrared signature.

Should Donald Trump sign the a pledge to support the eventual GOP nominee?
Why? Isn't it his right to support any person he wants? So, I guess my answer is no, that is, unless that what he chooses to do.

According to the article, Trump is required to sign a pledge that he will support the eventual GOP nominee if he wants to participate in the South Carolina primary.

This is an important issue to his campaign because if he doesn't sign it, he can't paticipate in the SC primary which will then make it difficult, if not impossible, for him to win the nomination.

On the other hand, if he does sign it, it will prohibit him from running as an independent third party candidate. He acknowledges this himself in the article.

Of course, there is the possibility that he could win South Carolina. But with this pledge, there is also the possibility that he could end his chances of getting elected president should he not prevail as the party's nominee at the GOP convention.

The dilemma is effectively forcing Trump's hand. It is an interesting strategy, too and could be a win-win for the GOP. If Trump declines to sign, and goes it alone as a third party independent, the GOP has political cover, effectively distancing themselves from him, which they cannot do now.

If he does sign, then the GOP can concentrate on using convention nomination rules to knock him out or even neutralize him as a potential threat come November 2016.

It is a really tough call which is why I posed the question.
